entities.name: Westbrook Secondary School
entities.summary: Secondary school introducing a phone-free school day policy from 3 September, following discussion with staff, students and the parents' council.

entities.name: Phone-free school day policy
entities.summary: Policy requiring students to lock phones in pouches on arrival, unlockable only at the end of the day, applied during lessons, breaks and lunch for all year groups.

entities.name: Parents and carers of Westbrook students
entities.summary: Addressees of the letter; some have concerns about travel and emergencies and are invited to raise them at an information evening or by email.

entities.name: Students of Westbrook Secondary School
entities.summary: Pupils aged 11-18 affected by the policy; surveyed last spring, with 64% reporting pressure to reply to messages and 41% having seen upsetting content on phones at school.

entities.name: Duarte
entities.summary: Pastoral lead at Westbrook Secondary who handles medical exemption requests (e.g. for students needing glucose monitoring) before 1 August.

entities.name: Students with medical needs relying on phones
entities.summary: Subset of students (e.g. those needing glucose monitoring) exempted from the phone-free policy if they contact the pastoral lead before 1 August.

entities.name: Sixth-form students
entities.summary: Students aged 16-18 who get a partial exemption, allowed to unlock phones in the sixth-form common room during free periods.

entities.name: Teachers of Westbrook Secondary School
entities.summary: School staff who report that lessons regularly stop because of phones, supporting the rationale for the new policy.

entities.name: Parents' council
entities.summary: Parent representative body consulted by the school during a year of discussion before adopting the phone-free policy.

entities.name: Amara Lewis
entities.summary: Headteacher of Westbrook Secondary School who signs the letter announcing and defending the new policy.

entities.name: Personal phone pouch
entities.summary: Lockable pouch (costing the school €18 each) in which students must lock their phones on arrival; only opened at unlocking stations at day's end.

entities.name: Nearby schools with phone-free policies
entities.summary: Three schools near Westbrook that adopted the same phone-free change last year and reported calmer breaks and fewer online bullying incidents during school hours.

entities.name: Information evening (17 June)
entities.summary: Meeting at Westbrook's main hall on Tuesday 17 June at 6:30pm where parents can raise concerns about the new policy, e.g. about travel and emergencies.

entities.name: Online bullying during school hours
entities.summary: Issue cited as a motivation for the policy; nearby schools with phone bans reported fewer such incidents after adopting similar rules.

entities.name: Student survey (spring)
entities.summary: Survey conducted last spring among Westbrook students that found 64% feel pressure to reply to messages during the school day and 41% had seen upsetting content on a phone at school.
